summary: Uses profile curves on spline surfaces to hide, reveal, untrim, or change the altitude of regions without deleting the underlying surface.

key_params.name: group
key_params.note: Surface/profile group or profile pattern to trim

key_params.name: optype
key_params.note: Keep outside, keep inside, keep natural, untrim, or change altitude

key_params.name: individual
key_params.note: Process trim profiles individually rather than as a combined region

key_params.name: bigloop
key_params.note: Explicitly build an outer trim loop for multi-step trim workflows

key_params.name: trimtol
key_params.note: Tolerance for treating trim curves and patch edges as intersecting

key_params.name: altitude
key_params.note: Altitude transition used by Change Altitude mode

common_gotchas: Trim hides surface regions instead of deleting the underlying surface, so hidden control points can still influence the visible surface.
Only surfaces that contain profile curves can be trimmed; use Project SOP or Carve SOP upstream to create profiles.
Open profiles outside a surface domain can make portions of the surface appear cut away.
Natural orientation depends on clockwise or counter-clockwise profile direction and may require an explicit outer trim loop.
When Process Profiles Individually is off, multiple loops may combine into only the first region the SOP can resolve.
key_concepts: Trim SOP uses profile curves on spline surfaces to keep, remove, untrim, or change altitude of surface regions.
Open and closed profiles are resolved in surface UV space and may be nested or extend outside the domain.
Overlapping trim loops use the winding rule, so overlapping commands accumulate rather than canceling out.
Project SOP or Carve SOP is usually needed upstream because only surfaces containing profile curves can be trimmed.
